Avoid an undeclared fundamental theorem of algebra: for weight mu the defining Casimir formula gives (Omega-c(mu))v=2 sum_{alpha>0,s} y_{alpha,s}x_{alpha,s}v, a finite sum of negative-root actions on vectors of strictly higher support weights. Induct on the finite upper support set and commute Omega through those root actions to obtain an annihilating polynomial for v that is a product of linear factors (t-c(eta)). Bezout polynomials for the finitely many relatively prime powers (t-a)^N give unique generalized-eigenvector components of v; prove this elementary identity by polynomial division, and use uniqueness to make the decomposition compatible as the annihilating polynomial grows. Hence V is the algebraic direct sum of its generalized eigenspaces. Centrality makes the global generalized eigenspaces submodules. Any primitive highest class of weight lambda in the a-summand is both annihilated by a power of Omega-a and an eigenvector of eigenvalue c(lambda)=(lambda+2rho,lambda), so c(lambda)=a. If dominant lambda>mu, write lambda-mu=sum n_i alpha_i. Then c(lambda)-c(mu)=sum n_i d_i(lambda(h_i)+mu(h_i)+2)>0, because d_i>0 and some n_i>0. Thus comparable distinct primitive weights cannot share a Casimir summand. The published rho convention and d_i normalization are used, not a positive-definite full Cartan form.
